root_cause.text: After load_segments() invalidates the GS base register, KCOV's instrumentation (which relies on per-CPU data accessed via GS) causes a crash when any instrumented C code is subsequently executed during kexec.
root_cause.evidence: "The load_segments() function changes segment registers, invalidating GS base (which KCOV relies on for per-cpu data). When CONFIG_KCOV is enabled, any subsequent instrumented C code call (e.g. native_gdt_invalidate()) begins crashing the kernel in an endless loop."

relevance_review.reason: The group disables KCOV instrumentation in machine_kexec_64.o, directly preventing the crash caused by GS base invalidation during kexec.

The vulnerability states that instrumented C code (via KCOV) crashes after the GS base register is invalidated during kexec. Disabling KCOV for physaddr.o directly prevents its code from being instrumented, thereby avoiding the described crash scenario. This aligns with the root cause by removing instrumentation from a file likely executed in the vulnerable code path.
